title: Fuse phases into one thread body

def fuse_phases(phases: list[list[str]], names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """phases[k]: the C statements of local loop k, which uses the variable names[k].
    Return the CUDA kernel body: each phase as { int32_t name = threadIdx.x; ...statements } then __syncthreads();"""
    out = []
    for stmts, n in zip(phases, names):
        out.append(f"for (int32_t {n} = 0; {n} < blockDim.x; {n}++) {{")

hints: The starter writes each phase as a loop over threads, which is the CPU's view. On a GPU every thread already exists: t is just threadIdx.x.
Wrap each phase in braces so its variable names don't clash with the next phase's.
End every phase with __syncthreads();, including the last: a phase inside a loop runs again, and the next round's first phase must not start before everyone finished.
prompt: In .uir a block's phases are consecutive local loops. In CUDA there's one thread body, and each thread runs every phase in turn, with a barrier between them. Write fuse_phases(phases, names): for each phase, a line {, a line int32_t NAME = threadIdx.x;, the phase's statements indented by two spaces, a line }, then a line __syncthreads();.

answer.code:
def fuse_phases(phases: list[list[str]], names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """phases[k]: the C statements of local loop k, which uses the variable names[k].
    Return the CUDA kernel body: each phase as { int32_t name = threadIdx.x; ...statements } then __syncthreads();"""
    out = []
    for stmts, n in zip(phases, names):
        out.append("{")
        out.append(f"  int32_t {n} = threadIdx.x;")
        out += ["  " + s for s in stmts]
        out.append("}")
        out.append("__syncthreads();")
    return out
answer.explain: This is the step that turns the .uir block into CUDA. On the CPU, a phase is a loop over thread indices. On the GPU, every thread runs the whole body and reads its own index from threadIdx.x, so the loop disappears, and the barrier takes its place: no thread starts phase 2 until all have finished phase 1. The reference also ends the last phase with a barrier, which matters when the phases sit inside a loop.
